title: 07. Google ADK: Day 3 — Runner, Sessions & Events: The Invocation Flow
summary: How a single user message becomes a stream of Events — and how to inspect, tune, and persist every step
objectives: The Event Class — Every Step is an Event

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
How a single user message becomes a stream of Events — and how to inspect, tune, and persist every step

Day 3 / 15
ADK v2.7.0 (Aug 2026)
Python 3.10+

🎯 Learning Objectives

- Construct a `Runner` with the right services for dev vs production

- Use `run_async()` to consume an `AsyncIterator[Event]` stream

- Inspect every `Event` field — including 2.0 additions `isolation_scope`, `node_info`, `output`

- Detect event types: tool call, tool result, partial text, final response, state delta

- Apply `RunConfig` for streaming mode, `max_llm_calls`, CFC, and context compression

- Build a multi-turn conversation with persistent `session.state` across runs

sections.title: 1. Why the Invocation Flow Matters
sections.body:
On Day 02 we built beautiful `LlmAgent` objects — but an agent that's never run is just a config object. The **Runner** is what turns config into behavior. It owns the event loop, fetches and persists the Session, dispatches the agent, and streams back a typed sequence of Events. Every production deployment is, at its core, a thin HTTP wrapper around `runner.run_async(...)`.

Consider what actually happens when a user types *"What's the weather in Tokyo?"* in your chat UI. The Runner (1) looks up the Session by `session_id`, (2) appends the user message as an Event with `author='user'`, (3) invokes the agent's `_run_async_impl`, (4) receives zero or more tool-call Events, (5) executes those tools (yielding more Events), (6) regenerates with tool results, (7) emits a final Event with `is_final_response() == True`, (8) writes the new state back to the SessionService, (9) yields the final Event to your `async for` loop. Miss any step and you'll get cryptic errors — or worse, silently wrong state.

**v2.7.0 (August 2026) made two changes you'll see today.** First, `Event` gained `node_info` and `output` fields in v2.0 — these matter as soon as you touch graph workflows (Day 12); knowing them now avoids a refactor later. Second, `RunConfig` exposes `context_window_compression` — long conversations no longer blow past the LLM's token limit; the runner transparently summarizes early turns. Today you'll see all of this in code, then build four progressively richer runners that exercise each concept.

💡 Key Concept

The Runner is **stateless across runs** — it loads fresh Session state from `session_service` on every `run_async()` call. This means horizontal scaling is trivial: any Runner instance can serve any user, as long as they share the same SessionService (InMemory for dev, Database/VertexAi for prod). The agent object is also safe to share — only the Session carries per-user state.

sections.title: 2. The Runner Class
sections.body:
### 2.1 Constructor — pick your services

```python
from google.adk.runners import Runner, InMemoryRunner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService

# Explicit construction (production-style — choose each service)
runner = Runner(
    agent=root_agent,
    app_name="my_app",
    session_service=InMemorySessionService(),
    # artifact_service=GcsArtifactService(bucket_name="..."),  # optional
    # memory_service=VertexAiMemoryBankService(...),            # optional
    # credential_service=...,                                    # optional
    # plugin_manager=PluginManager([MyPlugin()]),               # optional
)

# Convenience: InMemoryRunner bundles all InMemory services
runner = InMemoryRunner(agent=root_agent, app_name="my_app")
```

Every service is **pluggable**. For dev use `InMemoryRunner`. For prod, swap each service for a persistent implementation: `DatabaseSessionService` (SQLAlchemy), `VertexAiSessionService` (Agent Runtime), `GcsArtifactService` (Cloud Storage). The agent code stays identical — only the Runner wiring changes.

```
                         RUNNER ANATOMY
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  class Runner:                                                   │
│      # ── Constructor ────────────────────────────────────────   │
│      agent: BaseAgent              # your root_agent             │
│      app_name: str                                              │
│      session_service: BaseSessionService                        │
│      artifact_service: BaseArtifactService = None   # optional  │
│      memory_service:   BaseMemoryService   = None   # optional  │
│      credential_service = None       # for OAuth/API keys       │
│      plugin_manager = None           # cross-cutting plugins    │
│      context_cache_config = None     # context caching          │
│      resumability_config = None      # long-running run resume  │
│                                                                  │
│      # ── Public methods ────────────────────────────────────   │
│      run(user_id, session_id, new_message) -> Iterator[Event]   │
│      run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message,                │
│                run_config=None) -> AsyncIterator[Event]         │
│      run_live(...)                  # realtime audio/video      │
│      run_debug(...)                 # debug-mode traces         │
│      rewind_async(...)              # session rewind            │
│      close()                        # cleanup resources         │
│                                                                  │
│      # ── Convenience subclass ──────────────────────────────   │
│      InMemoryRunner(agent, app_name)                            │
│          # auto-creates InMemorySessionService,                 │
│          # InMemoryArtifactService, InMemoryMemoryService       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2.2 `run_async()` vs `run()`

| Method | Returns | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message, run_config=None)` | `AsyncIterator[Event]` | Default — non-blocking, scales to thousands of concurrent runs |
| `run(user_id, session_id, new_message)` | `Iterator[Event]` | Synchronous contexts (scripts, tests); internally wraps `asyncio.run()` |

Consume with `async for`:

```python
async for event in runner.run_async(
    user_id="u1", session_id="s1",
    new_message=types.Content(role="user", parts=[types.Part(text="Hi")]),
):
    if event.is_final_response():
        print(event.content.parts[0].text)
```

If you're in a sync script, use `asyncio.run(_main())` and define an `async def _main()` that does the `async for`. ADK's sessions are async-first; the sync `run()` is a convenience wrapper, not a faster path.

🚀 Pro Tip

**Always pair `asyncio.run()` with a single top-level `async def main()`.** Don't call `asyncio.run()` inside a loop — it creates and tears down a new event loop each call. For multi-turn chats, collect all turns inside one `async def` and call `asyncio.run()` once.

sections.title: 3. Sessions — The Per-Conversation State
sections.body:
A **Session** is the unit of conversation state: every message, every tool call, every state mutation for one user in one app belongs to exactly one Session. The SessionService stores and retrieves them.

### 3.1 Session fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | Unique session ID (you provide or let ADK generate) |
| `app_name` | `str` | App namespace — same as Runner's `app_name` |
| `user_id` | `str` | User identifier — same user can have many sessions |
| `state` | `State` | Dict-like, prefix-aware (`app:`/`user:`/`temp:`) |
| `events` | `list[Event]` | Chronological history — full audit log |
| `last_update_time` | `float` | Unix timestamp of last `append_event` |

### 3.2 Lifecycle

```python
# 1. Create (or reuse) a session
session = await session_service.create_session(
    app_name="my_app", user_id="u1", session_id="sess-001",
    state={"user:name": "Alice"},  # optional initial state
)

# 2. Run — the Runner fetches the session, runs the agent,
#    and appends all yielded Events to it automatically.
async for event in runner.run_async(
    user_id="u1", session_id="sess-001",
    new_message=user_content,
):
    ...

# 3. (Optional) append system events directly — e.g. a state update
#    from outside the agent loop:
from google.adk.events import Event, EventActions
import time
await session_service.append_event(
    session,
    Event(
        invocation_id="inv-1",
        author="system",
        actions=EventActions(state_delta={"user:login_count": 1}),
        timestamp=time.time(),
    ),
)

# 4. (Optional) Delete when done
await session_service.delete_session(
    app_name="my_app", user_id="u1", session_id="sess-001"
)
```

The Runner handles step 2's event-appending for you. Steps 1, 3, and 4 are explicit — call them from your application code.

```
STATE PREFIX SCOPE (Session.state dict)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  key (no prefix)   →  session-scoped   persists with DB/Vertex
  "user:key"        →  user-scoped      shared across user's sessions
  "app:key"         →  app-scoped       shared across all users
  "temp:key"        →  invocation-only  discarded after one turn
                                       shared across sub-agents
                                       via InvocationContext
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Examples:
    state["conversation_count"] = 5         # session
    state["user:preferred_lang"] = "en"     # user
    state["app:tenant_id"] = "acme"         # app
    state["temp:validation_needed"] = True  # this turn only
```

⚠️ Important

**`SessionNotFoundError`** — if you pass a non-existent `session_id` to `run_async`, the Runner raises. Mitigate by constructing `Runner(..., auto_create_session=True)` (sets `auto_create=True`) — the Runner will lazily create a session on first use. Useful for chat UIs where the session ID is minted client-side.

sections.title: 4. The Event Class — Every Step is an Event
sections.body:
`Event` extends `LlmResponse`. Every state change, tool call, tool result, partial text chunk, and final answer is yielded as an Event by `run_async()`. Inspecting Events is the single most useful debugging skill in ADK.

### 4.1 Fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | `Optional[types.Content]` | The payload — text, `function_call`, `function_response`, etc. |
| `author` | `str` | `'user'` for user messages, else the agent name |
| `invocation_id` | `str` | Groups all events in one `run_async` call |
| `id` | `str` | Unique event ID |
| `timestamp` | `float` | Unix timestamp |
| `actions` | `EventActions` | Side-effects: state_delta, transfer, escalate, ... |
| `partial` | `Optional[bool]` | `True` if this is a streaming chunk (not the final part) |
| `branch` | `Optional[str]` | Hierarchy path (for sub-agent trees) |
| `isolation_scope` | `Optional[str]` | **NEW 2.0** — restricts which agent contexts see this event |
| `long_running_tool_ids` | `list[str]` | IDs of paused long-running tools (final-response trigger) |
| `node_info` | `Optional[NodeInfo]` | **NEW 2.0** — workflow-node metadata |
| `output` | `Any` | **NEW 2.0** — generic data output from a workflow node |

### 4.2 `EventActions` — what the Event *does*

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `state_delta: dict[str, Any]` | Merge these into `session.state` |
| `artifact_delta: dict[str, int]` | `{filename: version}` for saved artifacts |
| `transfer_to_agent: Optional[str]` | Hand control to another agent |
| `escalate: bool` | Exit a `LoopAgent` immediately |
| `skip_summarization: bool` | Bypass the LLM's tool-result summarization |
| `end_of_agent: bool` | This agent is done — control returns to parent |
| `request_auth_configs: dict` | Ask the user for OAuth credentials |
| `route` | **NEW 2.0** — routing keys for conditional graph edges |
| `requested_tool_confirmations` | HITL approval requests |
| `rewind_before_invocation_id` | Session rewind marker |
| `set_model_response` | Override the model's response |
| `compaction` | Context-window compaction marker |
| `render_ui_widgets` | Trigger frontend UI widgets |

```
EVENT LIFECYCLE
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  User sends message
        │
        ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Event #1  author='user'         │   content = user message
  │           actions=None          │
  └────────────┬────────────────────┘
               ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Event #2  author='weather_agent'│   content = function_call
  │           actions=None          │   (LLM wants to call tool)
  └────────────┬────────────────────┘
               ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Event #3  author='weather_agent'│   content = function_response
  │           actions=state_delta=  │   (tool returned)
  │             {"temp:cold": True} │
  └────────────┬────────────────────┘
               ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Event #4  author='weather_agent'│   content = final text
  │           actions=None          │   is_final_response() = True
  │           partial=False         │
  └─────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 5. is_final_response() — The Most-Called Method
sections.body:
Returns `True` when **any** of:

1. `actions.skip_summarization is True` — the agent explicitly opted out of further processing
2. `long_running_tool_ids` is non-empty — the run is paused for human-in-the-loop
3. **Or all** of:
   - No function calls in the content
   - No function responses in the content
   - Not `partial` (i.e. this is the complete response, not a streaming chunk)
   - Doesn't end with a code-execution result

```python
async for event in runner.run_async(...):
    if event.is_final_response():
        final_text = event.content.parts[0].text
        print("🟢 Final:", final_text)
```

**Common bug**: forgetting that partial streaming events have `partial=True` and are *not* final. If you print every event's text, you'll see character-by-character chunks; only the one where `is_final_response()` returns `True` is the complete answer.

💡 Key Concept

The `is_final_response()` check is the **only** reliable way to detect "the agent is done speaking." Checking `event.content.parts[0].text` truthiness, or `event.author != 'user'`, will both fail in edge cases (tool-call events have no text; partial chunks have text but aren't final). Always use `is_final_response()`.

sections.title: 6. Event Detection Patterns
sections.body:
```python
async for event in runner.run_async(...):
    print(f"Event from: {event.author}")

    if event.content and event.content.parts:
        # ── Tool call (LLM wants to invoke a tool) ──
        if event.get_function_calls():
            for fc in event.get_function_calls():
                print(f"  → tool call: {fc.name}({fc.args})")

        # ── Tool result (tool returned a value) ──
        elif event.get_function_responses():
            for fr in event.get_function_responses():
                print(f"  ← tool result: {fr.name} = {fr.response}")

        # ── Text (partial stream chunk OR final) ──
        elif event.content.parts[0].text:
            kind = "streaming chunk" if event.partial else "complete text"
            print(f"  ✎ {kind}: {event.content.parts[0].text!r}")

    # ── Pure state/artifact side-effect ──
    elif event.actions and (event.actions.state_delta or event.actions.artifact_delta):
        print(f"  ⤷ state_delta: {event.actions.state_delta}")
        print(f"  ⤷ artifact_delta: {event.actions.artifact_delta}")

    # ── Control signal (transfer, escalate, auth request, ...) ──
    else:
        print(f"  ⊙ control: {event.actions}")
```

This pattern catches every Event type. Print this snippet on a sticky note — you'll use it for every debugging session.

🚀 Pro Tip

The `get_function_calls()` and `get_function_responses()` methods return `None` if the content has no such parts, so the `if` checks double as both type-tests and presence-checks. They're safer than indexing into `event.content.parts[0]` directly, which can raise `IndexError` on empty content.

sections.title: 7. RunConfig — Per-Run Tuning
sections.body:
While `generate_content_config` (Day 02) tunes the **LLM**, `RunConfig` tunes the **Runner** — how it streams, how many LLM calls it allows per turn, how much history to load. Pass as the `run_config=` kwarg on every `run_async()`.

```python
from google.adk.agents.run_config import RunConfig, StreamingMode
from google.adk.sessions.base_session_service import GetSessionConfig

config = RunConfig(
    streaming_mode=StreamingMode.SSE,             # NONE | SSE | BIDI
    max_llm_calls=200,                            # hard cap per run
    support_cfc=True,                             # experimental — compositional function calling
    get_session_config=GetSessionConfig(num_recent_events=50),  # limit loaded history
    # context_window_compression=...,             # auto-summarize old turns
    # include_thoughts_from_other_agents=False,
    # model_input_context=[types.Content(...)],   # per-turn context, not persisted
    # speech_config=types.SpeechConfig(...),
    # response_modalities=["AUDIO", "TEXT"],
)
async for event in runner.run_async(..., run_config=config):
    ...
```

### 7.1 Streaming modes

| Mode | Behavior | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `StreamingMode.NONE` | One Event with the complete response | Batch jobs, non-interactive |
| `StreamingMode.SSE` (default) | Server-Sent Events: partial text chunks then a final | Chat UIs with typing indicator |
| `StreamingMode.BIDI` | Bidirectional — full duplex audio/video | Voice agents, live API |

### 7.2 `max_llm_calls` — circuit breaker

Each LLM round-trip counts. If the agent falls into a tool-call loop, `max_llm_calls=200` stops it. Default is generous; lower it (`10`–`20`) for cost-sensitive or untrusted workloads.

### 7.3 `get_session_config` — history window

`GetSessionConfig(num_recent_events=50)` loads only the last 50 events into the LLM context, preventing token-limit blowups on long conversations. Pair with `context_window_compression` for truly unlimited history (auto-summarizes older turns).

⚠️ Important

**`max_llm_calls` counts *LLM calls*, not *tool calls*.** A single user turn can trigger multiple LLM rounds (call tool → regenerate → call another tool → regenerate → final). Set `max_llm_calls` low enough to fail fast on loops but high enough for legitimate multi-step work — `10` is a safe default for chat agents.

sections.title: 9. Mermaid: Session Lifecycle & Event Flow
sections.body:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User / Client
    participant R as Runner
    participant SS as SessionService
    participant A as Agent (LlmAgent)
    participant L as LLM
    participant T as Tools

    U->>R: run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message)
    R->>SS: get_session(session_id)
    SS-->>R: Session (state + events history)
    R->>SS: append_event(user_message_event)
    R->>A: _run_async_impl(ctx)
    A->>L: generate_content_async(contents, config)
    L-->>A: function_call (e.g. get_weather)
    A-->>R: yield Event(tool_call)
    R->>T: execute_tool(args)
    T-->>R: tool_result dict
    R-->>R: append_event(tool_response_event)
    A->>L: regenerate with tool_response
    L-->>A: final text
    A-->>R: yield Event(final_text, is_final=True)
    R->>SS: append_event(final_event) — persists state_delta
    R-->>U: yield Event(final)
```

Notice the **two regeneration cycles** in this diagram — the LLM is called twice. The first call returns a tool call; the second (after the tool result is appended) returns the final text. Each call is one tick against `max_llm_calls`.

```
USER MESSAGE
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   Runner    │  ← run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message)
└──────┬──────┘
       │ fetches Session (state + events history)
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   Agent     │  ← _run_async_impl(ctx)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│ before_model_cb │  ← optional guardrail / cache
└────────┬────────┘
         │ None → continue
         ▼
┌─────────────┐
│     LLM     │  ← generate_content_async(contents, config)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│ after_model_cb  │  ← optional response modification
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
   ╔═══════════════╗
   ║  Tool call?   ║
   ╚══════╤════════╝
      YES │           NO
          ▼            ▼
   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
   │ run tool │   │ yield Event  │ ← is_final_response() = True
   └────┬─────┘   └──────────────┘
        ▼
   ┌──────────────┐
   │ after_tool_cb│
   └──────┬───────┘
          ▼
   loop back to LLM
```

diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as Your code
  participant R as Runner
  participant S as SessionService
  participant A as LlmAgent
  participant T as Tool
  App->>R: run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message)
  R->>S: get_session, append user Event
  R->>A: run with InvocationContext
  A-->>R: Event - function_call get_weather
  R->>T: execute tool
  T-->>R: Event - function_response
  A-->>R: Event - final text, state_delta
  R->>S: append_event (commits state_delta)
  R-->>App: async stream of Events, last one is_final_response()
diagrams.explain: `runner.run_async()` yields **Events** as they happen: tool calls, tool responses, partial text and the final response. State changes travel inside `event.actions.state_delta` and are **committed only when the Runner appends the event** to the session — so always change state through context/EventActions, never by mutating a session object you fetched.

sections.title: 10. Four Progressive Examples
sections.body:
We'll build four runners, each adding capability:

1. **Minimal** — single query, single final response
2. **Streaming inspector** — print every Event with its type
3. **RunConfig tuning** — SSE streaming, `max_llm_calls`, history window
4. **Multi-turn chat** — state persists across runs in the same Session

Example 1: Minimal Runner — Single Query, Single Response

The shortest possible end-to-end ADK program: build agent, build session, build runner, run, print final.

This is the absolute minimum to get a real `run_async` call working. Three things to notice:

1. `asyncio.run()` wraps the whole flow — ADK is async-first.
2. The user message is a `types.Content` with `role='user'` and a `Part(text=...)` — this is the canonical LLM input format across Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
3. `event.is_final_response()` filters out tool-call and partial events so we only print the answer.

Everything you build later in the course will reuse this skeleton; the only changes are richer agents, richer event handling, and persistent session services.

```python
# example_01_minimal_runner.py
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os

from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from google.adk.runners import Runner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService
from google.genai import types

# ── 1. Agent ──────────────────────────────────────────────
def get_current_time(city: str) -> dict:
    """Return the current time in a city.

    Args:
        city (str): The city name.
    """
    import datetime
    return {"city": city, "time": datetime.datetime.utcnow().strftime("%H:%M UTC")}

agent = LlmAgent(
    name="time_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Tells the current time in a city.",
    instruction="Use get_current_time to answer. Be concise.",
    tools=[get_current_time],
)

# ── 2. Session + Runner ───────────────────────────────────
APP_NAME = "time_app"
USER_ID = "u1"
SESSION_ID = "s1"

session_service = InMemorySessionService()
runner = Runner(agent=agent, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)

async def main() -> None:
    # Create session (auto_create_session=True would skip this)
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
    )

    # Build user message
    user_msg = types.Content(
        role="user",
        parts=[types.Part(text="What time is it in Tokyo?")],
    )

    # Run — single async for-loop
    async for event in runner.run_async(
        user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID, new_message=user_msg,
    ):
        if event.is_final_response() and event.content:
            print("🟢 Final:", event.content.parts[0].text.strip())

# os.environ["GOOGLE_API_KEY"] = "..."   # set your key
asyncio.run(main())
```

**Output**

```text
🟢 Final: It's currently 14:32 UTC in Tokyo. (Note: Tokyo is UTC+9, so local time is 23:32 — the tool returns UTC for simplicity.)
```

💡 Key Concept

**`InMemorySessionService` is dev-only.** State lives in the Runner's process memory and is lost on restart. For production, swap to `DatabaseSessionService("sqlite+aiosqlite:///./sessions.db")` (or Postgres/MySQL) — same code, persistent storage. We'll cover this in depth on Day 08 (Session Services).

Example 2: Streaming Event Inspector — Print Every Event with Type

The debug loop you'll paste into every ADK project: classify each Event as tool call, tool result, partial text, final, or side-effect.

This is the most useful snippet in the entire course. Whenever an agent misbehaves — calls the wrong tool, returns truncated text, gets stuck in a loop — the answer is in the Event stream. This example classifies every event into one of five buckets and prints a structured trace.

The agent is a multi-tool travel assistant so we get tool calls AND tool results AND a final synthesis — all the interesting event types in one run.

```python
# example_02_event_inspector.py
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from google.adk.runners import Runner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService
from google.genai import types

def get_weather(city: str) -> dict:
    """Return mock weather for a city.

    Args:
        city (str): City name.
    """
    data = {"Tokyo": {"temp_c": 22, "condition": "Partly Cloudy"},
            "London": {"temp_c": 15, "condition": "Rainy"}}
    d = data.get(city, {"temp_c": 20, "condition": "Clear"})
    return {"city": city, **d}

def get_population(country: str) -> dict:
    """Return mock population for a country.

    Args:
        country (str): Country name.
    """
    pops = {"Japan": 125_800_000, "UK": 67_500_000}
    return {"country": country, "population": pops.get(country, "unknown")}

agent = LlmAgent(
    name="city_info_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Answers city info: weather + country population.",
    instruction=(
        "Use get_weather and get_population to answer multi-part city questions. "
        "Synthesize a single natural-language answer at the end."
    ),
    tools=[get_weather, get_population],
)

APP_NAME, USER_ID, SESSION_ID = "city_app", "u1", "s1"
session_service = InMemorySessionService()
runner = Runner(agent=agent, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)

def classify_event(event) -> str:
    """Return a human-readable label for any Event."""
    if event.content and event.content.parts:
        if event.get_function_calls():
            names = [fc.name for fc in event.get_function_calls()]
            return f"TOOL_CALL({', '.join(names)})"
        if event.get_function_responses():
            names = [fr.name for fr in event.get_function_responses()]
            return f"TOOL_RESULT({', '.join(names)})"
        if event.content.parts[0].text:
            return "STREAM_CHUNK" if event.partial else "COMPLETE_TEXT"
    if event.actions and (event.actions.state_delta or event.actions.artifact_delta):
        return f"DELTA(state={list((event.actions.state_delta or {}).keys())})"
    return "CONTROL"

async def main() -> None:
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
    )
    user_msg = types.Content(
        role="user",
        parts=[types.Part(text="What's the weather in Tokyo, and what's Japan's population?")],
    )
    print(f"{'#':>3}  {'AUTHOR':18}  {'TYPE':22}  DETAIL")
    print("-" * 80)
    n = 0
    async for event in runner.run_async(
        user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID, new_message=user_msg,
    ):
        n += 1
        label = classify_event(event)
        detail = ""
        if "TOOL_CALL" in label:
            fc = event.get_function_calls()[0]
            detail = f"{fc.name}({fc.args})"
        elif "TOOL_RESULT" in label:
            fr = event.get_function_responses()[0]
            detail = f"{fr.name} → {fr.response}"
        elif label == "COMPLETE_TEXT":
            detail = event.content.parts[0].text[:60].replace("\n", " ") + "..."
        elif label == "STREAM_CHUNK":
            detail = event.content.parts[0].text[:40].replace("\n", " ")
        final = "  ★ FINAL" if event.is_final_response() else ""
        print(f"{n:>3}  {event.author:18}  {label:22}  {detail}{final}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Output**

```text
#  AUTHOR              TYPE                   DETAIL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1  user                COMPLETE_TEXT          What's the weather in Tokyo, and what...
  2  city_info_agent     TOOL_CALL(get_weather)  get_weather({'city': 'Tokyo'})
  3  city_info_agent     TOOL_RESULT(get_weather) get_weather → {'city': 'Tokyo', 'temp_c': 22, 'condition': 'Partly Cloudy'}
  4  city_info_agent     TOOL_CALL(get_population) get_population({'country': 'Japan'})
  5  city_info_agent     TOOL_RESULT(get_population) get_population → {'country': 'Japan', 'population': 125800000}
  6  city_info_agent     COMPLETE_TEXT          Tokyo is currently 22°C and partly clo...  ★ FINAL
```

### What the trace tells you

Six events for one user question. Reading the trace:

1. **Event 1** — the user message itself, auto-appended by the Runner.
2. **Event 2** — LLM's first response: a `function_call` for `get_weather`. (LLM call #1.)
3. **Event 3** — Runner executes the tool and appends the result as a `function_response`. (No LLM call yet.)
4. **Event 4** — LLM's second response: another `function_call`, this time for `get_population`. (LLM call #2.)
5. **Event 5** — Runner executes the second tool, appends the result.
6. **Event 6** — LLM's third response: final synthesized text. (LLM call #3.) `is_final_response()` returns `True` — note the `★ FINAL` marker.

So this run used **3 of the default `max_llm_calls=200`** — well within budget. If you saw a trace with 50+ events, you'd know the agent was looping.

🚀 Pro Tip

Wrap `classify_event()` in a tiny utility module and import it everywhere. When something breaks, drop `from debug_utils import trace_run; await trace_run(runner, ...)` into your script and instantly see the full event stream. This saves hours over the course of a project.

Example 3: RunConfig Tuning — SSE Streaming, `max_llm_calls`, History Window

Apply `RunConfig` to control streaming behavior, cap LLM calls, and limit how much history the Runner loads.

This example exercises three `RunConfig` knobs:

1. **`streaming_mode=StreamingMode.SSE`** — partial text chunks arrive as `partial=True` Events. Without this, you'd get one Event with the complete response (fine for batch, bad for chat UX).
2. **`max_llm_calls=10`** — fail-fast circuit breaker. The agent has at most 10 LLM round-trips per turn; if it loops, the run aborts with a clear error.
3. **`get_session_config=GetSessionConfig(num_recent_events=20)`** — only the last 20 events are loaded into the LLM context, preventing token blowups on long conversations.

Notice how partial streaming changes the Event stream: instead of one Event 6 with the complete text, you see many small Events (one per token or word chunk), all with `partial=True`, ending with one final Event where `partial=False` and `is_final_response()` returns `True`.

```python
# example_03_runconfig.py
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from google.adk.agents.run_config import RunConfig, StreamingMode
from google.adk.runners import Runner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService, GetSessionConfig
from google.genai import types

def get_stock_price(ticker: str) -> dict:
    """Return mock stock price.

    Args:
        ticker (str): Stock symbol like 'AAPL'.
    """
    prices = {"AAPL": 226.84, "GOOG": 178.12}
    return {"ticker": ticker, "price_usd": prices.get(ticker, 100.0)}

agent = LlmAgent(
    name="stock_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Fetches stock prices with brief commentary.",
    instruction=(
        "Fetch the price with get_stock_price, then write a 2-3 sentence market commentary."
    ),
    tools=[get_stock_price],
    generate_content_config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.3, max_output_tokens=300,
    ),
)

APP_NAME, USER_ID, SESSION_ID = "stock_app", "u1", "s1"
session_service = InMemorySessionService()
runner = Runner(agent=agent, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)

async def main() -> None:
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
    )

    # ── RunConfig — three knobs at once ──────────────────
    config = RunConfig(
        streaming_mode=StreamingMode.SSE,  # partial chunks
        max_llm_calls=10,                  # circuit breaker
        get_session_config=GetSessionConfig(num_recent_events=20),
    )

    user_msg = types.Content(
        role="user", parts=[types.Part(text="What's AAPL trading at?")],
    )

    n_partial = 0
    final_text = ""
    print("── streaming trace ──")
    async for event in runner.run_async(
        user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
        new_message=user_msg, run_config=config,
    ):
        if event.partial and event.content and event.content.parts[0].text:
            n_partial += 1
            print(f"  chunk {n_partial:2d}: {event.content.parts[0].text!r}")
        if event.is_final_response():
            final_text = event.content.parts[0].text

    print(f"\n── summary ──")
    print(f"  partial chunks:  {n_partial}")
    print(f"  final text len:  {len(final_text)} chars")
    print(f"  final answer:    {final_text}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Output**

```text
── streaming trace ──
  chunk  1: 'AAPL'
  chunk  2: ' is currently'
  chunk  3: ' trading at'
  chunk  4: ' $226.84'
  chunk  5: '. The stock'
  chunk  6: ' has seen'
  chunk  7: ' steady demand'
  chunk  8: ' this quarter'
  chunk  9: ', with analysts'
  chunk 10: ' maintaining a'
  chunk 11: ' buy rating.'

── summary ──
  partial chunks:  11
  final text len:  127 chars
  final answer:    AAPL is currently trading at $226.84. The stock has seen steady demand this quarter, with analysts maintaining a buy rating.
```

⚠️ Important

**`StreamingMode.BIDI` requires a Live API-compatible model** (e.g. `gemini-2.0-flash-live-001`) and the `run_live()` method, not `run_async()`. Use BIDI only for real-time voice/video agents — covered on Day 15.

Example 4: Multi-Turn Chat — State Persists Across Runs

Three sequential `run_async` calls against the same Session — the agent remembers the user's name and prior topic.

The Runner is stateless across runs, but the **Session** persists between runs (in `InMemorySessionService`, in memory; in `DatabaseSessionService`, in the DB). This example issues three sequential user messages against the same `session_id`, with no agent rebuild between them. Each run sees the full prior history.

The agent uses an `output_key="topic"` to auto-save the user's last topic to `session.state["topic"]`. On the third turn, we read that state back to verify it persisted across run boundaries.

```python
# example_04_multi_turn.py
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from google.adk.runners import Runner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService
from google.genai import types

agent = LlmAgent(
    name="chat_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Multi-turn chat agent that remembers context.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a friendly conversational agent. "
        "Refer back to prior turns when relevant. "
        "Be concise (1-2 sentences)."
    ),
    output_key="last_response",  # auto-save final text to state
    generate_content_config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.4, max_output_tokens=200,
    ),
)

APP_NAME, USER_ID, SESSION_ID = "chat_app", "u1", "sess-001"
session_service = InMemorySessionService()
runner = Runner(agent=agent, app_name=APP_NAME, session_service=session_service)

async def send(message: str) -> str:
    """Send one user message, return the agent's final text."""
    user_msg = types.Content(role="user", parts=[types.Part(text=message)])
    final = ""
    async for event in runner.run_async(
        user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID, new_message=user_msg,
    ):
        if event.is_final_response() and event.content:
            final = event.content.parts[0].text.strip()
    return final

async def main() -> None:
    # Create session with initial state
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
        state={"user:name": "Alice"},
    )

    # ── Turn 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────
    r1 = await send("Hi! I'm Alice. I'm learning ADK today.")
    print(f"Turn 1 → {r1}")

    # ── Turn 2 — refers back to turn 1 ───────────────────
    r2 = await send("What did I just say I was learning?")
    print(f"Turn 2 → {r2}")

    # ── Turn 3 — refers back to turn 1's name ────────────
    r3 = await send("What's my name again?")
    print(f"Turn 3 → {r3}")

    # ── Inspect persisted state ───────────────────────────
    session = await session_service.get_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME, user_id=USER_ID, session_id=SESSION_ID,
    )
    print(f"\n── session.state ──")
    print(f"  user:name:      {session.state.get('user:name')}")
    print(f"  last_response:  {session.state.get('last_response', '')[:60]}...")
    print(f"  total events:   {len(session.events)}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Output**

```text
Turn 1 → Nice to meet you, Alice! ADK is a great choice — good luck with your learning today.
Turn 2 → You said you're learning ADK (Google's Agent Development Kit) today.
Turn 3 → Your name is Alice.

── session.state ──
  user:name:      Alice
  last_response:  Your name is Alice.
  total events:   6
```

💡 Key Concept

**`output_key="last_response"` saved Turn 3's text to `session.state["last_response"]`.** Any downstream agent (in a sub-agent tree, a sequential workflow, or a later turn) can read it via `{last_response}` templating. This is the canonical pattern for inter-agent data passing — no manual plumbing.

Also note `total events: 6` — three user messages + three final responses. Each turn added exactly two Events to the history. The agent has full visibility into all six on every turn.

🚀 Pro Tip

**The Session ID is the conversation ID.** Mint it client-side (UUID) when a user opens a chat, store it in their browser, and reuse it for the entire conversation. To "start a new conversation", mint a new Session ID and stop using the old one — no need to delete (though `delete_session` is good hygiene).

sections.title: Day 3 Summary
sections.body:
📌 Key Takeaways

- **The `Runner` is the orchestrator — construct it with `agent`, `app_name`, and a `session_service`; `InMemoryRunner` bundles dev-friendly defaults**

- **`run_async()` returns an `AsyncIterator[Event]` — consume with `async for`; use `run()` only in sync scripts**

- **Sessions carry per-conversation state across runs — the Runner is stateless, but the Session persists (in memory for dev, DB/Vertex for prod)**

- **Every step is an `Event`: tool calls, tool results, partial text chunks, control signals. `get_function_calls()` / `get_function_responses()` classify them**

- **`is_final_response()` is the only reliable way to detect 'agent is done' — it returns `True` on `skip_summarization`, long-running pauses, or no-tool-calls-and-not-partial**

- **`EventActions` carries side-effects: `state_delta`, `artifact_delta`, `transfer_to_agent`, `escalate`, `skip_summarization`, `route` (new in 2.0)**

- **`RunConfig` tunes the Runner: `streaming_mode` (NONE/SSE/BIDI), `max_llm_calls` circuit breaker, `get_session_config` history window, `context_window_compression`**

- **v2.0 added `isolation_scope`, `node_info`, and `output` to `Event` — these matter as soon as you touch graph workflows (Day 12)**
